what_its_for: This medicine combines two drugs in one tablet. Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that relieves pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis (such as rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis). Famotidine is an acid reducer that is added to help protect your stomach from ulcers that ibuprofen can sometimes cause.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or split the tablet. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food or milk may help if you feel stomach upset. Stay upright (sitting or standing) for at least 10 minutes after taking it. Take this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed.
dosing: The usual adult dose is ONE tablet taken THREE times a day. Try to space your doses evenly throughout the day (for example, morning, afternoon, and evening). Do not take more tablets than your doctor told you to, and do not take it more often than prescribed. Each tablet contains 800 mg of ibuprofen and 26.6 mg of famotidine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in a dry place, away from heat and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Safely dispose of any unused or expired tablets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other NSAIDs (such as aspirin, naproxen, or celecoxib) while using this medicine unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as combining them raises your risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase your risk of stomach bleeding. Avoid taking more than directed. Do not use this medicine right before or after heart bypass surgery (CABG). Limit prolonged sun exposure, as NSAIDs may increase sun sensitivity in some people.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: black, tarry, or bloody stools; vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds; severe stomach pain; chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden weakness (signs of a heart attack or stroke); sudden vision changes; swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue (signs of a serious allergic reaction); unusual weight gain or swelling in your legs; little or no urination; or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Also contact your doctor if you develop a skin rash, your pain gets worse, or your symptoms do not improve.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some pain and inflammation relief within a few hours of your first dose. For the best results with arthritis, it usually takes a few days to 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit. The famotidine in this tablet works right away to help protect your stomach lining.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): You may be at higher risk for stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and heart-related side effects. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy: Do NOT use this medicine at 20 weeks of pregnancy or later unless specifically directed by your doctor, as it can harm the unborn baby. Avoid use after 30 weeks of pregnancy entirely. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine while breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: This medicine may not be safe if you have significant kidney or liver disease. Your doctor will decide if it is appropriate for you. Children: This medicine is approved for adults only and should not be given to children.
